lens: Drawing appeal, contour and scale simplification
independence: Recorded before reading another review or score.
observedStrengths: The original refined raster has an appealing hierarchy: huge cream head, quiet compact torso, broad paired wing shapes and unequal antenna paddles. The vector interpretation preserves that innocent construction and recognizable color grouping without requiring surface texture.

identity.png shows a useful head-only application. Across the presented avatar ladder, the head and unequal paddles remain the principal identity signals; the face is generously spaced at larger sizes.

poses.png shows worthwhile staging improvements. Lowering the free mitten in thinking and separating the focused mittens makes the hands less likely to read as extra ruff scallops. These are drawing improvements achieved through posing.

The updated night antenna edge restores visible stem continuity in identity.png. all-24.png retains a coherent character across affectionate, surprised, sleepy and angry expressions without enlarging the body or adding anatomical features.

concreteConcerns.observation: The ruff, wrist connections and two mittens still form a dense necklace of similarly weighted loops in grateful, shy and several neutral-adjacent poses. At the contact-sheet scale, individual hand intentions become subordinate to that cluster.
concreteConcerns.evidence: poses.png grateful/updated; all-24.png Grateful, Shy and Worried; character.js ruff and mitten paths use outlines close in weight to the torso.
concreteConcerns.implication: Prioritize deliberate overlaps and a small patch of clear torso around each meaningful gesture; do not enlarge hands or lengthen arms.

concreteConcerns.observation: The night treatment keeps the antenna attached but introduces a conspicuous double contour around its paddles at header scale. The night full-body examples also appear softer around their edges than the day versions.
concreteConcerns.evidence: identity.png updated/night and night GitHub header; character.js uses a 16-unit antenna edge plus a root drop-shadow filter.
concreteConcerns.implication: Compare local edge treatments at both avatar and header sizes before retaining one universal treatment. This is a contour/material question, not evidence that more glow is needed.

concreteConcerns.observation: The raster's broad, softly shaded forms and the vector's comparatively uniform contour produce different tactile impressions. That difference alone is not a defect, but adding texture would not resolve the actual overlap and scale issues above.
concreteConcerns.evidence: heynag-moth-v5-refined.png compared with identity.png and poses.png.
concreteConcerns.implication: Keep the original master intact and name the native asset as an interpretation. Evaluate contour rhythm before considering any material variation.

qualityCriteriaForNine: At intended avatar sizes, the asymmetrical antenna construction stays connected and the face stays readable in both themes; use actual-size exports, not enlarged inspection alone.
At full-body sizes, held key poses have intentional hand/ruff separation or clearly intentional contact, without stray dark knots or false appendages.
Day and night preserve identical geometry and numeric poses, while edge treatment remains quiet at both 96–160px applications and larger headers.

Any refinement demonstrably improves a specific reading problem against the current version while preserving tiny anatomy, four layered wings and the original appeal. Detail quantity is not an acceptance criterion.
highestValueExperiment: Make one tightly controlled comparison sheet: current treatment versus pose/overlap cleanup for thinking, grateful and worried, plus a restrained local night-edge alternative. Hold anatomy, palette and timing fixed. Inspect at actual 96/128/160px full-body sizes and one large header size. Adopt only changes with a visible clarity gain; do not add grain, fur marks, broad glow or new anatomy.
limits: Static supplied evidence and source inspection only; contact sheets may be rescaled by the viewer. No live motion, perceptual testing or audience recognition measurement. This is an independent AI drawing review, not final-art approval.
